_comment: Terms for the lesson mass-society. status: ok = attested in a Turkish source I opened; chosen = my own rendering (no Turkish source checked); check = plausible but needs a Turkish-language reviewer. Existing glossary terms (opinion-leader, two-step-flow, filter-bubble, magic-bullet, suggestibility, spiral-of-silence, mass-media, mass-communication) are used exactly as in content/terminology/*.json. Keys are concept ids or short slugs.

mass-society.note: 'Kitle toplumu' is in the course unit title and in Baylarov & Rustamli 2022 (kitle toplumu kavramı). 'Kitle toplumu kuramı' comes from the course title.

crowd-psychology.note: Turkish sources use 'kitle' for both crowd and mass, and Le Bon's book is 'Kitleler Psikolojisi' or 'Kitlelerin Psikolojisi' (Polat & Durmuş 2015; Aktürkoğlu 2021). The lesson uses 'kalabalık' for crowd to keep it apart from 'mass' (kitle) and says so on the glossary card.

public-vs-crowd.note: No established Turkish rendering of Tarde's 'public' was found in a source I opened. 'Kamu' is chosen and glossed at first mention; 'halk' and 'izleyici kitlesi' were not used because they blur the distinction.

tyranny-of-the-majority.note: Both forms are in use: Turkish Wikipedia has 'Çoğunluğun tiranlığı'; a Turkish selection from Amerika'da Demokrasi is titled 'Çoğunluğun Zorbalığı' (Cumhuriyet Kitap, 2020).

atomisation.note: Natural rendering of 'atomization'; not checked in a Turkish source.

intermediate-groups.note: Kornhauser's 'intermediate groups / structures'. 'Ara gruplar' and 'aracı kurumlar' are possible alternatives, not checked.

mass-culture-fear.note: The course unit title says 'Kitle Kültürü'; 'korkusu' is the lesson's own framing of the aristocratic and left worries about culture.

mass-man.note: Ortega's 'hombre-masa'; English 'mass-man' as in the excerpts read. Turkish translations of the book have several titles: Kitlelerin Ayaklanması (İş Bankası Kültür Yayınları), Kitlelerin İsyanı, Kütlelerin İsyanı, and 'Kitlelerin Yükselişi' in one article.

accessibility-availability.en: accessibility of elites / availability of non-elites (masses)
accessibility-availability.note: Kornhauser's formula in my own wording; the Turkish course books were not checked for a fixed rendering.

tutelary-power.note: 'Tutelary' is Reeve's word in the Gutenberg translation; 'yumuşak despotluk' is used only descriptively (Tocqueville himself says 'mild', and that the old words despotism and tyranny do not fit).

one-step-flow.note: Built on the glossary term 'iki aşamalı iletişim akışı' (two-step flow of communication).

primary-group.note: Used as in Kornhauser's entry ('primary relations'); not checked in a Turkish source.
